transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

In fact, if the drum gets very hot but clothes remain damp, the heat is working and the issue is usually airflow or load size. The most common cause for this symptom on Samsung washer-dryers is simply overloading the drying cycle (drying a full wash load) or a blocked lint filter/condenser restricting air circulation. Less commonly, it could be a faulty thermal cut-out or heater element if no heat was generated at all. To narrow this down safely: 1) Was the laundry load for drying roughly half the machine's washing capacity (e.g., max 5kg)? 2) Did the drum get noticeably hot during the dry phase, or did it stay only warm/cool?
No, I load a full 9kg drum and it washes and dries in one go. The drum does get hot during drying, and the clothes are hot but damp at the end.

The issue is that you are drying a full 9kg load; washer-dryers can only dry about half their wash capacity (around 5–6kg for this model). Drying a full load leaves clothes damp because there isn't enough space for air to circulate properly. To fix this, split your laundry: wash the full 9kg, but only put up to 5kg in the drum for the drying cycle. If you still have issues with smaller loads, check the lint filter and condenser (usually behind a flap at the bottom front) are clean.
